pluss::note::from_lines¶

Back to Note Factory API Reference

Signatures¶

Note pluss::note::from_lines(string_view text, bool keep_ends = false,
                             bool drop_empty = false)

Split One String Into A Column Of Lines¶

from_lines() takes a single string and returns a rank-1 Note with one cell per line. It is the standard way to turn a file’s contents, a multi-line message, or a block of log text into an addressable text column that Note methods can then process row by row.

Lines are separated by the newline character \n. A \r before a \n is not stripped — carriage returns stay in the cell text; normalise line endings first if that matters. The final segment is emitted whether or not text ends with \n.

Parameters¶

  • keep_ends — when false (default) the \n separators are removed from every cell. When true, each cell keeps its trailing \n (the last segment keeps one only if text ended with \n). Use keep_ends = true when you intend to re-join the lines and want the original breaks back exactly.

  • drop_empty — when true, empty segments (a \n immediately followed by another \n, or a leading/trailing blank line) are omitted entirely, so blank lines never become cells. Default false keeps them as "" cells.

The result is always rank 1 and UTF-8 mode. An empty input yields a zero-length Note.

Splitting is on raw \n bytes, so this is safe for UTF-8 text — multi-byte characters are never split.

Example 1: Basic Line Split¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::note::from_lines("alpha\nbeta\ngamma"))
          << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["alpha", "beta", "gamma"]

Three lines, separators removed.

Example 2: A Trailing Newline Adds No Empty Cell¶

const pluss::Note n = pluss::note::from_lines("alpha\nbeta\n");
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["alpha", "beta"]

The \n at the end terminates the last line rather than starting an empty one.

Example 3: Blank Lines Become Empty Cells By Default¶

pluss::note::print(std::cout, pluss::note::from_lines("alpha\n\ngamma")) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["alpha", "", "gamma"]

The \n\n produces an empty middle cell.

Example 4: Dropping Blank Lines¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::from_lines("alpha\n\ngamma", false, true)) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["alpha", "gamma"]

drop_empty = true removes the empty segment.

Example 5: Keeping The Line Endings¶

const pluss::Note n = pluss::note::from_lines("alpha\nbeta", true);
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["alpha\n", "beta"]

Each interior line keeps its \n. "beta" has none because the input did not end with one. (print shows the newline as the escape \n; the cell holds a real newline byte.)

Example 6: An Empty Input¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::note::from_lines("")) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[0], dim=1, numel=0, encoding=utf8)
[]

A zero-length rank-1 Note, not a scalar.

See Also¶

  • pluss::note::from_words: split on runs of whitespace instead of on line breaks.

  • pluss::note::make: build a column from strings you already hold separately.

  • pluss::note::format: assemble a string; pair with from_lines to round-trip.
